answer: A farm needs 12 physical roots per batch and cannot clone them, which turns a software cost into a procurement one. Because the whisper measurement is attested to the orchard verifier, the relic audit records each device and an extracted key fails to sign. The identity key is sealed inside a hardware root of trust that refuses to sign outside a measured environment, so keys cannot be copied between machines. That is 40 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
